description: MAR-527 made `verifier_passed` a field the kernel READS from a verdict document the reviewer WRITES, instead of a claim the coordinator relayed. The invariant that makes it a verdict rather than a self-report -- `passed` must equal 'no blocking finding' -- is not expressible in JSON Schema and is enforced by acs_lib.verdict.validate_verdict, which is what the SubagentStop hook runs. These cases pin that meaning, in both directions, plus the freshness rules that stop a stale verdict from opening the create-pr gate and the two fields ADR-0099 makes a review owe the loop: the commit it judged, and what a fix must make true.

cases.title: an honest pass is accepted
cases.note: ADR-0099 retired the sixteen-dimension table the old title counted ("over all 15 base dimensions"): a verdict is a list of findings, and a pass is an empty one. ADR-0097 keys the document to the run, so the reply names `run_id` where it named `ticket_id` and the document lives under runs/<id>/steps/code/iter-1/.

cases.title: HEADLINE: passed=true alongside a blocking finding is refused
cases.note: The defect MAR-527 exists to remove. A verifier that claims to pass while carrying a blocking finding must not be able to open the create-pr gate. The rule is untouched by the redesign; ADR-0099 only changes how the refusal names the offender -- a finding id (`F-1-1`), because an id is what crosses the loop, where a dimension name was all the old document had.

stderr_contains: passed is true but the verdict carries 1 blocking finding(s) (F-1-1)
`passed` is derived from the findings, not asserted alongside them

cases.title: an honest fail -- passed=false with the blocking finding recorded -- is accepted
cases.note: Unchanged in force. ADR-0099 gives the finding the three fields the loop runs on -- `id`, `evidence`, `resolved_when` -- so the fixture carries them and validate_verdict now requires them.

cases.title: the invariant binds in both directions: passed=false with no blocking finding is refused
cases.note: A verifier cannot fail a run without saying what blocks it -- otherwise the review loop has nothing to converge on. The wording is unchanged; ADR-0097 only moves where the document is read from.

stderr_contains: passed is false but no finding is `blocking`
record the blocking finding that fails the verdict, or report the pass

cases.title: an `advisory` finding is carried but never gates
cases.note: ADR-0099 closes the severity enum to blocking|advisory: `info` was the dimension-era spelling of the same idea and is gone. A `needs-context` adjudication lands here rather than being dropped, which is what makes the non-gating severity load-bearing.

cases.title: FRESHNESS: another run's verdict is refused even on the right path
cases.note: A verdict is evidence only for the run that produced it -- copying a clean one into place must not open the gate. ADR-0097 makes the run, not the ticket, the thing it is evidence for, so the freshness axis is `run_id`.

stderr_contains: verdict run_id is 'TKT-9' but this is 'TKT-1'
a verdict is evidence only for the run that produced it

cases.title: FRESHNESS: `verdict show` refuses a verdict from another iteration
cases.note: Was a known_divergence through v0.4.9: cmd_verdict_show called validate_verdict without `skill` or `iteration`, so a document whose own iteration was 1 read as a clean pass at iteration 3's path. MAR-573 passes both arguments through, closing it. The case pins the rule rather than the gap -- the refusal reaches stderr AND no passing verdict leaks to stdout, because the original defect's harm was a body reporting passed:true, not the exit code alone. ADR-0097 moves the iteration from the filename into the directory (steps/code/iter-3/verdict.json).

stderr_contains: verdict iteration is 1 but this is 3
a verdict is evidence only for the run that produced it

cases.title: FRESHNESS: `verdict show` refuses a verdict from another skill
cases.note: The other axis of the same gap, closed by the same one-call change in MAR-573. Was a known_divergence through v0.4.9. Under ADR-0097 the skill names a step directory under the run, so the axis survives verbatim.

stderr_contains: verdict skill is 'docs-sync' but this is 'code'
a verdict is evidence only for the run that produced it

cases.title: a missing verdict is reported, not treated as a pass
cases.note: The subject survives verbatim; ADR-0097 moves the path it reports from the ticket partition to runs/<id>/steps/code/iter-1/verdict.json, so the case now pins that path as well as the refusal.

cases.title: a lens verdict validates under its own lens
cases.note: ADR-0099 keeps the five lenses (A-E) and retires the per-lens dimension subsets the old title counted ("its own 5 dimensions, not all 16"): a lens reports findings, and what is judged per lens is that the document declares the lens it was written for.

cases.title: a verdict with no `reviewed_sha` is refused
cases.note: Replaces VERDICT-006's completeness rule with the v0.5.0 form of the same question -- did the review do what it owed? ADR-0099 answers it with the commit the review judged: /acs:code copies `reviewed_sha` into result.json and diffs from it, so a verdict without one cannot say what it reviewed and the next iteration has no baseline.

stderr_contains: reviewed_sha is required and must be a non-empty string
it is the baseline /acs:code diffs from

cases.title: a `confirmed` finding with no `resolved_when` is refused
cases.note: The other half of VERDICT-015's retired subject. ADR-0099 makes `resolved_when` the adjudicator's refutation criterion restated as an exit criterion: a confirmed finding without one tells /acs:code to fix something without saying when it is fixed, which is how a review loop fails to converge.

stderr_contains: is confirmed but carries no resolved_when
that field is what /acs:code works to
